text:
mira: seeing weird IOPS stalls on gpool nodes in us-west-2, GPUs stuck provisioning because kubelets report container start slow -> eviction spike :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
jonas: any SMART warnings? or just latency?
sasha: got a dpkg alert earlier, but current node g-23 shows reallocated sectors bump + heavy write amplification from training jobs
kevin: here's the pattern i see: ephemeral-cleaner backlog grows, TRIMs aren't being issued quickly because the cleaner hands off to a central job that is starved. NVMe queue depth goes crazy -> io wait -> kubelet times out.
mira: repro steps: start a big finetune (checkpoint churn) and simultaneously create many tiny containers on same node, within ~10m the node latency spikes and new pods get Evicted/ContainerStartFailed.
jonas: logs from ephemeral-cleaner on g-23 snapshot:

```
2026-03-17T09:12:03Z ephemeral-cleaner[1]: scanned=812 files, queued=812
2026-03-17T09:12:04Z ephemeral-cleaner[1]: handoff to gc-worker-0 delayed: queue-depth=1200, worker-busy=1
2026-03-17T09:12:05Z kernel: nvme0n1: I/O 12345 QID 0 timeout
2026-03-17T09:12:06Z kernel: EXT4-fs (nvme0n1p1): delayed allocation failed
```

sasha: ops-bot shows fstrim not running because systemd timer missed on nodes with high load
kevin: i pushed a short-term mitigation: reduce ephemeral-cleaner batch_size from 200 -> 40 and enable async-trim flag on cleaner config, rolling update started on the pool.
mira: can we defang long-running checkpoint writers onto network-store instead of local? cost tradeoff though.
jonas: quick commands i ran to triage:

```
# check evictions
kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector=status.phase=Failed -o wide | grep Evicted
# fstrim test (on node)
sudo fstrim -v /mnt/ephemeral
# cleaner logs
journalctl -u ephemeral-cleaner -n 200 --no-pager
```

infra-bot: alert: node g-23 nvme_trim_missed=47 in 1h, autoscale-protect applied
kevin: rolling update finished on 6/8 nodes, two nodes still hitting high write amplification; planning to cordon them and run `fstrim` + `smartctl -a` overnight.
sasha: also adding backpressure in scheduling: make pod creation for heavy-checkpoint jobs require local-ssd=exclusive so we don't co-locate many writers.
mira: ops question — is there a way to make the cleaner do incremental TRIMs under load instead of batching big syncs?
jonas: yes, cleaner supports incremental-trim-window and async-trim; i recommended window=30s and enable async in config. that'll lower instantaneous IO but increase total trim ops (acceptable).
kevin: longer-term: two options — enlarge ephemeral partitions (costy), or move checkpoints to NFS/netstore for heavy training. for now i'll push config change + schedule maintenance for cordoned nodes 0300 UTC.
ops-bot: scheduled maintenance for nodes [g-21,g-23] at 2026-03-18T03:00Z, action: cordon -> fstrim -> smartctl -> uncdrain
mira: leaving notes for SRE runbook to add these checks to node health: nvme write amplification > 3 && trim_missed > 10 => auto-cordon.
sasha: also add GPU provisioning fallback to avoid trying to schedule on nodes with recent trim_missed alerts. cheap policy change.
jonas: confirmed metrics to track: nvme_write_amp, trim_missed_count, ephemeral_cleaner_queue, pod_start_latency. I'll add dashboards.
kevin: after rolling update pod start latency normalized on 6 nodes; two nodes still showing slow disk IO -> maintenance overnight.
mira: thanks all. follow-up: patch cleaner config in staging first and run heavy checkpoint job to validate. :thumbsup:
